old_title: Pakistan v Sri Lanka: tri-series cricket one-day international final - live
new_title: Pakistan v Sri Lanka: tri-series cricket one-day international final - as it happened
old_text:
50th over: Sri Lanka 325-8 (Asitha 7, Theekshana 7) Rauf starts with two dots, Theekshana wriggles about and picks up a single. A leg bye off the fourth, a single from the fifth , and small disagreement between the batters, which is very well fielded on the rope, and two from the last, actually one as Asitha didn't ground his bat. Well hauled back Pakistan, who took six wickets in the last ten overs.
49th over: Sri Lanka 321-8 (Asitha 5, Theekshana 7) Naseem with the penultimate over. It's a mixed bag. He starts with a Arachchige's wicket, throws in a couple of wides, Theekshana smashes six down the ground and Asitha toe ends four to finish.
Dean Kinsella is back: "Oh no Tanya. It seems I bigged up SL too soon. I thought they were gonna get 350 minimum. I should know by now to say nothing!" Me too, this really has been a limp to the line, but Pakistan haeve been excellent at the death."
48th over: Sri Lanka 307-7 (Arachchige 15, Theekshana 2) Rauf has been super today. Arachchige pulls him over midwicket for four, but Wellalage is wicket number two. Theekshana ducks into a bouncer and is clattered on the helmet, picks up a couple and passes a concussion test. A slow over rate means only four fielders will be allowed outside the 30 yard circle for Pakistan's last two overs.
47th over: Sri Lanka 299-6 (Arachchige 10, Wellalage 2) Some of the stands at this lovely cricket bowl are nearly full now, the noise levels rising. More so as Liyannage fails to reach the rope. Sri Lanka will pass 300 but not get a sniff of what looked possible at half way.
46th over: Sri Lanka 291-5 (Liyanage 6, Arachchige 3) Shaheen pulls out a fast reversing yorker from his bag of tricks, but Arachchige keeps it out. Immaculate over, just four from it.
45th over: Sri Lanka 285-5 (Liyanage 3, Arachchige 1) An eventful over from Rauf that started with Liyange taking a nasty blow on the back/neck via a wild throw from Shaheen, who apologises immediately. Ooof that must have hurt. Somehow, he's good to continue. Then the wicket, and just five from the over. Good comeback by Pakistan who now have two new batters at the crease.
44th over: Sri Lanka 282-4 (Rathnayake 77, Liyanage 1) Shaheen fancies two in a row, but it's a terrible review. Three singles follow. Shanaka will be fuming to miss the finale.
43rd over: Sri Lanka 278-3 ( Rathnayake 75, Shanaka 17) Haris Rauf's first ball is tonked through extra cover for four by Rathnayake, his third glided away by Shanaka. Super running by Sri Lanka turns one to two. A third four is whipped off Shanaka's boots. Fifteen from the over.
42nd over: Sri Lanka 263-3 ( Rathnayake 70, Shanaka 7) Shaheen nails three yorkers, but Shanaka isn't hanging about and with the theatrical swish of a curtain, slams him over long on for six - his tenth of the tournament. Only Harry Brook (12 ) has more. After Kamindu was out, Shaheen raced to shake his hand before he walked off.
One trick too many, as Kamindu tries to scoop a yorker and misses. He reviews, but to no avail, hit on the front boot and umpire's call. What a debut century!
41st over: Sri Lanka 255-2 (Kamindu 131, Rathnayake 69) Rathnayake is on the charge, sweeping two fours brutally, then Kamindu tucks into a low full toss, one bounce over the rope. Worse, it's a no ball, but he can only mine one off the free hit, which is pulled straight to long on.
40th over: Sri Lanka 238-2 (Kamindu 126, Rathnayake 58) Naseem Shah with his eighth over, crouches at the top of his run, wipes his sweat away. And there's the scoop, a reverse, done on the move with style, but only for two. A run-out chance as Kamindu turns back midway down the pitch but the throw misses. Ten overs left as a fading sun has one last blaze.
39th over: Sri Lanka 232-2 (Kamindu 122, Rathnayake 55) Sri Lanka can't get Arafat away to the rope but still pick up six from the over.
An email drops. Hello Dean Kinsella! "Wow. Just tuned in after following the Saffers destroying Oz this morning. So this is looking like a mammoth total for Sri Lanka. They must be considered serious contenders for the world cup next year. And nothing would please me more." Wouldn't that be a cracking narrative? So impressed with their batters, not only the shotmaking but also the composure.
38th over: Sri Lanka 226-2 (Kamindu 120, Rathnayake 52) Dusk is falling over Lahore, the sky a sleepy peach. Kamindu, feet perfectly balanced, pulls Naseem over deep midwicket as if he's waving away the butler. Rathnayake brings up his fifty with a dab off the hips.
36th over: Sri Lanka 210-2 (Kamindu 112, Rathnayake 44) Farheem again, long run up, long sleeves. On TMS, Steven Finn says in this scenario England would be looking for the scoops but, as it turns out, Rathnayake doesn't need to - he flames a short ball to the rope then drives, divinely, on the up, off the back foot to bring up the 100 partnership. The current run rate is just under six an over.
35th over: Sri Lanka 200-2 (Kamindu 111, Rathnayake 35) Haris Rauf seems the most likely, and Shaheen keeps him on. We pause after one ball as Mendis gets an elongated arm massage and a pickle juice. The umpires, in tight-fitting florescent pink, are unimpressed. A top edge flies through where first slip might have hovered.
34th over: Sri Lanka 193-2 (Kamindu 105, Rathnayake 34) With feeling! Upper cuts Faheem for four to bring up three figures, blows out his lips in relief and raises bat in one hand, helmet in the other, to the dressing room where Gary Kirsten leads the applause. Lovely innings, unhurried, but off just 107 balls.
33rd over: Sri Lanka 185-2 (Kamindu 99, Rathnayake 32) After a pause for more drinks, they resume at the Gaddafi stadium. Haris Rauf is brought back with Kamindu just three short of his first ODI century. There he must remain for another over but Rathnayake, nimble footed, hauls four with style.
32nd over: Sri Lanka 176-2 (Kamindu 97, Rathnayake 25) In the Tepal tea lounge, four immaculate looking Pakistan fans serenely sip. Ah, Faheem Ahraf for the first time today. He keeps it tight for five balls, Kamindu pulls his last, which is heading to the rope but well fielded in the deep.
31st over: Sri Lanka 171-2 (Kamindu 94, Rathnayake 23) Pakistan aren't letting Sri Lanka charge into the distance, but two wides from Shaheen are not ideal in an over that has already leaked six.
29th over: Sri Lanka 159-2 (Kamindu 88, Rathnayake 19) Shaheen brings himself back on, Pakistan really could do with getting Kamindu out rapidly. The 50 partnership comes up in 44 balls as a huge kite drifts across the ground, in and out of the Lahore mist.
28th over: Sri Lanka 154-2 (Kamindu 86, Rathnayake 15) Kamindu, the most relaxed man in the world, oils his wrists and sends Arafat spilling through the covers for four.
27th over: Sri Lanka 146-2 (Kamindu 80, Rathnayake 14) Naseem pushes his luscious hair back off his face while Shaheen stretches. A fierce bouncer beats Kamindu who just pulls out of a hook in time. Good over.
26th over: Sri Lanka 142-2 (Kamindu 78, Rathnayake 12) Arafat Minhas comes back, ushers his fielders into position with a wave of the hand. Sri Lanka are cautious, respectful.
Australia, incidentally, are four down in the thriller at Cape Town after an over eager Cameron Green runs out Josh Inglis.
25th over: Sri Lanka 138-2 (Kamindu 75, Rathnayake 11) Glorious from Rathnayake, who frying pans Naseem for four off the front foot over mid-on. A pretty drive deserves four but is cut off. The ground is busier now, plenty of people walking up and down the aisles.
24th over: Sri Lanka 128-2 (Kamindu 73, Rathnayake 3) Kamindu gets into position like a whippet and reverse sweeps four past backward point, he follows up with another boundary, this time just gently directed to deep third. Salman, previously economical, is not pleased.
23rd over: Sri Lanka 118-2 (Kamindu 64, Rathnayake 2) Shaheen saves some Haris Rauf for later and brings back Naseem Shah. He nearly picks up Kamindu as well, but a drive lands just short of extra cover.
22nd over: Sri Lanka 114-2 (Kamindu 61, Rathnayake 1) A catch that looks better with each replay! Kamindu picks up four off the last ball of the over with a turn of the bat.
new_text:
I think we can all agree that tri-tournaments are a much better spectacle than bilateral series, this one has thrown up some brilliant moments and genuinely thrilling matches. That was a suitably fitting final, both sides were in it for the entire game until Minhas and Nawaz showed the mettle to get Pakistan home.
Pakistan win by three wickets and take the tri-series trophy!
Bosh! Shaheen slams a SIX over midwicket to seal victory for his side! That's a brilliant chase - the joint-highest in an ODI final. The crowd are jubilant and the players stream onto the pitch too. This means plenty.
WICKET! Arafat Minhas c & b AM Fernando 61 (Pakistan 324-6)
... and then he gets out. What a shame, he deserved to be there at the end but a mis-timed pull is claimed by the bowler and Minhas has to walk off with the finish line tantalisingly close.
47th over: Pakistan 308-5 (Nawaz 36, Minhas 45) Shot! Madushanka goes full and Arafat Minhas is waiting for it, lofting a hold the pose check drive over mid on for SIX. That's the shot of the evening and you sense Sri Lanka know the jig us up now. Nawaz gets in on the act with a squared drive for four. What a partnership this has been, Pakistan were wobbling but they rebuilt calmly and are now taking them over the line in style.
46th over: Pakistan 295-5 (Nawaz 31, Minhas 38) That's the big over that could seal it for Pakistan! Minhas clears the front leg and maaaaarmalises a SIX off Shanaka into the stands behind the midwicket boundary. Nawaz dabs deftly for four and in total fifteen crucial runs come off the 46th over. That leaves Pakistan red hot favourites with 31 needed to win off 24 balls. Sri Lanka need to go bang bang bang (bang bang).
45th over: Pakistan 280-5 (Nawaz 25, Minhas 29) Four singles off Fernando's first four balls and the umpires decide it is time for a change of ball. Maybe this one will hoop around corners? Not if pitched there - Arafat drills Fernando down the ground for four and bunts a full bunger for two to make it ten off the over. Rinse and repeat five times and Pakistan are home.
That's a crucial fifty partnership stand between this pair too. 46 needed from 30 balls.
44th over: Pakistan 270-5 (Nawaz 21, Minhas 23) Theekshana is bowled out, six runs off his final over leave him with figures of 1-57. Asitha Fernando is coming back into the attack with three overs up his sleeve. Time to strike. 56 from 36.
43rd over: Pakistan 264-5 (Nawaz 21, Minhas 17) Pakistan get their first boundary in over ten overs and it needed a mis-field at cover to help them on their way. Minhas drives and two becomes four. 62 from 42.
42nd over: Pakistan 257-5 (Nawaz 18, Minhas 13) Pakistan are sputtering here, they still can't find the fence and the worm is only getting taller. Wellalage finishes his ten with 1-58.
41st over: Pakistan 249-5 (Nawaz 15, Minhas 8) I've just raided my five year old's trick or treat sweet supply in anticipation of a spicy finish. The Skittles should kick in soon. 77 off 54...
40th over: Pakistan 244-5 (Nawaz 13, Minhas 5) No boundary for seven overs and counting, Pakistan just dealing in singles, Sri Lanka licking their lips. We're into the last ten overs so another fielder can patrol the deep.
39th over: Pakistan 238-5 (Nawaz 10, Minhas 2) The runs have dried up and the bowling and fielding is much tighter. Just three runs off Wellalage's ninth over, we're going to the wire folks, ain't no thang. 88 from 66. Five wickets remaining... put a couple wickets on that.
38th over: Pakistan 235-5 (Nawaz 8, Minhas 1) Sri Lanka sense their moment and tighten the screws just a little. Theekshana goes over, goes round and limits the runs to just five off the over. The required rate is up at eights.
37th over: Pakistan 230-5 (Nawaz 4, Minhas 0) Two new batters at the crease now for Pakistan, Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz. 96 needed from 78 balls, I reckon this is going to get squeaky.
35th over: Pakistan 224-4 (Agha 13, Nawaz 2) Wellalage rattles through an over for just four runs. 102 needed off 90 balls. A flutter of wickets would make things very interesting.
34th over: Pakistan 220-4 (Agha 11, Nawaz 0) Hasan Nawaz joins Salman Agha in the middle. Pakistan need 106 runs from 96 balls. Might we see a twist in the tale in the next hour or so? I wouldn't rule it out.
WICKET! Fakhar Zaman b Madushanka 127 (Pakistan 220-4)
Gone! Is it now? Fakhar charges down and misses, stumps splattered. The crowd rise to acknowledge a fantastic and potentially tri-tournament winning century.
33rd over: Pakistan 216-3 ( Fakhar Zaman 124, Agha 10) Fakhar is in a hurry now, he pulls and cuts for two fours off Wellalage. It's now or never for Sri Lanka, they have to get him out to get a sniff.
32nd over: Pakistan 204-3 ( Fakhar Zaman 113, Agha 10) Stop the clock. Fast eh? Fakhar slams the first ball back after the drinks break for SIX. Only a single off the rest of Madushanka's over but Pakistan look to be strolling this. Ahem.
31st over: Pakistan 197-3 ( Fakhar Zaman 106, Agha 10) Wellalage back into the attack with his fifth over. Four singles picked off without fuss and time for a drink. I'm going to make a rapid cup of Kenco... time me time me!
30th over: Pakistan 193-3 ( Fakhar Zaman 104, Agha 8) There it is! Fakhar Zaman brings up his century in style with a rasping pull shot off Asitha Fernando. The ball flies like a tracer bullet to the square leg boundary, Fakhar removes his helmet, salutes the crowd and then drops to his knees in prayer. 83 balls for his 12th ODI ton and he's given his side a huge chance at winning this tri-tournament.
28th over: Pakistan 174-3 ( Fakhar Zaman 91, Agha 2) Asitha Fernando back into the attack. Have a look? Nah. Fakhar dances down and slams him for SIX. Fernando does well to limit the damage to eleven runs from the over.
27th over: Pakistan 163-3 ( Fakhar Zaman 82, Agha 0) Can Sri Lanka get themselves back into this final? Salman Agha is the new batter, Pakistan need 163 from 23 overs.
WICKET! Saad Baig c & b Theekshana 74 (Pakistan 163-3)
Fakhar Zaman sweeps Theekshana for four and then bunts him down the ground for another. A single brings Baig on strike... GONE!
Caught and bowled chance chipped back and Theekshana grasps it. My word Sri Lanka needed that. A shame for Baig who batted beautifully and had a maiden ODI ton in his sights, he gave that away cheaply in the end.
26th over: Pakistan 154-2 ( Fakhar Zaman 73, Saad Baig 74) Shanaka goes short but Baig once again shows his command of the pull shot by bisecting the field on the leg side. A compact drive for two makes it nine off the over. Sri Lankan heads are beginning to go down.
25th over: Pakistan 145-2 ( Fakhar Zaman 70, Saad Baig 68) Now then! Theekshana spills a sharp return catch from Fakhar and that's a tough but very take-able chance gone begging. The sort of chance Sri Lanka need to take to get themselves back into this final. The previous two balls had been hit for consecutive boundaries too, that hurts. Ten runs off the over.
24th over: Pakistan 135-2 ( Fakhar Zaman 61, Saad Baig 67) Fakhar is mostly using brute force and power whereas Baig is finding the boundaries with deft touches. More than one way to ice a run chase. Shanaka offers a smidge of width and is run down to deep third for four by Baig. Touch.
23rd over: Pakistan 128-2 ( Fakhar Zaman 59, Saad Baig 62) Pedal meet metal? Fakhar dances down the track to Wellalage and hits him into the stands at midwicket. The pitch looks even paced with plenty of true bounce, ominous signs for Sri Lanka.
22nd over: Pakistan 119-2 ( Fakhar Zaman 52, Saad Baig 60) The 100 partnership is duly notched and Fakhar then goes to his 20th ODI half century with a meaty smear for four into the leg side. He's doing the business when it really matters again.
